paragrafos: **Three measurements side by side, never added together.** Two prediction markets (Polymarket and Kalshi), voting-intention polls checked against the official notice filed with the Commission des sondages, and French press coverage. The first round is on April 18 and the runoff on May 2, 2027.

**On 11/15/2026, the two markets and the polls measure different things about Marine Le Pen.** In the win contract, Polymarket pays 46.45 and Kalshi 52.00. In polls with fieldwork up to 11/10, she is first in all 61 first-round lists of the last 45 days, from 8 pollsters, at 27% to 38%, and leads in the 29 runoff match-ups in which she was tested, at 52% to 70%. Her appeal to the Cour de cassation against her ineligibility is due to be ruled on by early April 2027.

**Jean-Luc Mélenchon is 2nd in the poll average and 3rd in the Polymarket win contract.** In the polls, he averages 17.4 across 36 lists from 6 pollsters over the last 30 days and places in the top two in 55 of the 61 lists of the last 45 days; in the 10 runoff match-ups in which he was tested, he trails in all of them, at 30% to 34%. In the win contract, he is at 13.50 on Polymarket and 13.00 on Kalshi.

**Two names among the top five in both markets appear in fewer than half of the lists in the poll database: David Lisnard in 20 of the 61 of the last 45 days, and Christine Lagarde in 2.** Lisnard is 2nd on Polymarket, at 15.90, and at 15.00 on Kalshi; in the polls, he does not place in the top two in any of his 20 lists and averages 7.7 across 15 lists from 6 pollsters over the last 30 days. Lagarde is 4th on Polymarket, at 7.60, and at 6.00 on Kalshi; the two lists that test her are by Cluster17 for Politico, with fieldwork on 11/09 and 11/10, and give her 14% and 8%. Lagarde is not a declared candidate; on 10/29, the European Central Bank announced that she will leave the bank's presidency on 02/07/2027. Teddy Riner, who announced his candidacy on 11/09, is 6th on Polymarket, at 2.25, and at 2.00 on Kalshi; he appears in 1 of the 61 lists, also by Cluster17, at 2%, and the OpinionWay poll for CNews and the Elabe poll for BFMTV and La Tribune Dimanche, with fieldwork up to 11/13, which also test him, are not yet in the database.

**Édouard Philippe and Raphaël Glucksmann are close in the poll average and far apart in the Polymarket win contract.** Philippe averages 13.8 over the last 30 days, across 25 lists from 6 pollsters, and Glucksmann 13.3, across 34 lists from 6 pollsters; in the lists of the last 45 days in which they appear, Philippe places in the top two in 3 of 41, and Glucksmann in 3 of 56. In the win contract, Philippe is at 6.50 on Polymarket and 5.30 on Kalshi, and Glucksmann at 1.65 and 4.00.

**In the French press on 11/15, four of the ten headlines in the latest collection, from 6 outlets, are about Édouard Philippe.** franceinfo, BFMTV and Le Figaro report new proposals from his programme, among them building 4 million additional homes in ten years, and Le Figaro asks whether the fear of repeating what happened to Alain Juppé in 2016 lies behind his refusal to enter the primary. franceinfo reports that Marine Tondelier says "all those who want to bring us down support Marine Le Pen", citing the support of Donald Trump and Elon Musk for the candidate. BFMTV runs a commentary on Teddy Riner's result in a poll. Ouest-France runs the Restos du Cœur charity's appeal ahead of the election and a report from Châteaubriant, one of the poorest towns in Loire-Atlantique; Le Monde runs a piece on the "Fractures françaises" study, according to which the presidential election is no longer seen as a solution; and Les Echos runs a piece on "la campagne pop-corn".

**What this screen does not do.** It does not add or average the two markets, it does not turn a price into a voting intention, and it does not show a poll number without its checked official notice. On the Saturday and Sunday of each round, polls and prices are frozen, as French law of 1977 requires.
